scenes.fullText: Some duels are won by strength, and some by clever moves, but this one works differently, because here you do not destroy your enemy, you calm them down, and that is why it is called PACIFY.
Two players sit at one green table, and the game has seven rounds, and before it starts each player is dealt seven cards, and at the end the higher total score wins the whole thing.

There are nineteen cards in the game, twelve number cards that go from power one to power twelve, and seven trick cards, and those are gimmick cards, because when you play them, each one does something different to the game.

Now look at the number cards, because every one of them is good or bad, the bad cards are the red ones, going from Bandit at one up to Demon at eleven, and the good cards are the white ones, going from Paladin at two up to Angel at twelve.

Every round works the same way, you and the enemy each pick one card and put it down face down, then the cards flip over, so for example the Wizard at six meets the Ogre at three, and since six is bigger than three, the three points of difference go to you.

Let us play a real round together, you look at your seven cards and pick the Leviathan, a bad card with power nine, and put it down face down, the enemy puts one down too, and when they flip, the enemy has the Knight at four, so nine against four leaves a gap of five, five points go to you, and your total goes up.

But there is one big exception, if both cards are the same type, good and good, or bad and bad, the round is voided and nobody scores, so the good Valkyrie at eight against the good Wizard at six gives zero points.

On top of the number cards there are seven trick cards, and you can hold three at most, and they never fight with power, they do strange things to the rules instead, so let us go through them one by one.
The first trick is Void, and it erases the whole round, whatever was played is gone, and nobody gets anything.

The next trick is Eclipse, and it shuts down the round, and it also turns off the same-type rule, so while Eclipse is active, good cards and bad cards can hurt each other, and the bigger power still wins.
The Ward blocks any trick the enemy plays and pays you five points, but be careful, because against a normal number card the Ward is just a five, and it loses.
The Echo is a trade, you give up the round you are in, and in return the next round counts twice, so you lose a little now to win double later.
The Oracle lets you secretly look at two cards in the enemy hand, so you stop guessing and start planning.
The Reversal waits for the round to end, and then it swaps the two total scores, so what the enemy built becomes yours.

And then there is the Executioner, a card with zero power, and its job is punishment, because if the enemy plays a number card with power seven or higher, their whole score drops to zero, but if the enemy plays anything weaker, the Executioner just loses like any weak card.

And after the seventh round the game is over, and the player with the higher score wins, and in this game winning is called pacifying, so deal your cards, take your seat, and go pacify your first enemy.
